# implicit-sdf.library: DistanceToCircle

**Status:** Supported (tier `geometry`). In a shipping tier; the lint, type-check, and code-generation gates cover it. No release promises its signature yet.

## Summary

> The signed distance from a point to a circle of the given radius centred at
> the origin. Exact. (IQ: sdCircle.)

## Signature

```plato
DistanceToCircle(p: Point2D, radius: Number): Number
```

## Laws

These are declared laws. Whether each one passes is recorded by the law runner ([stdlib/VERIFICATION.md](../../../../../stdlib/VERIFICATION.md)), not by this page.

### Law_DegenerateCapsule2DIsCircle

[stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato, line 43](../../../../../stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato#L43)

```plato
// A planar capsule with coincident endpoints is a circle.
Law_DegenerateCapsule2DIsCircle(p: Point2D, radius: Number): Boolean
    => DistanceToCapsule(p, Point2D(0.0, 0.0), Point2D(0.0, 0.0), radius)
        .LawEq(DistanceToCircle(p, radius));
```

### Law_ZeroThicknessRingIsUnsignedCircle

[stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato, line 55](../../../../../stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato#L55)

```plato
// A ring of zero thickness is the unsigned distance to its centre circle: the
// ring is inside-out on both sides of the curve, so the sign cancels.
Law_ZeroThicknessRingIsUnsignedCircle(p: Point2D, radius: Number): Boolean
    => DistanceToRing(p, radius, 0.0).LawEq(DistanceToCircle(p, radius).Abs);
```

### Law_ExtrudedCircleIsCappedCylinder

[stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato, line 89](../../../../../stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato#L89)

```plato
// Extruding a circle along Z is a capped cylinder about Z — the same solid the
// spatial primitive describes about Y, so the axes are swapped to compare.
Law_ExtrudedCircleIsCappedCylinder(p: Point3D, radius: Number, halfHeight: Number): Boolean
    => ExtrudedDistance(DistanceToCircle(Point2D(p.X, p.Y), radius), p.Z, halfHeight)
        .LawEq(DistanceToCappedCylinder(Point3D(p.X, p.Z, p.Y), halfHeight, radius));
```

### Law_RevolvedCircleIsSphere

[stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato, line 95](../../../../../stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato#L95)

```plato
// Revolving about the Y axis with no offset sends a point to its distance from
// that axis, so a revolved planar circle centred on the axis is a sphere.
Law_RevolvedCircleIsSphere(p: Point3D, radius: Number): Boolean
    => DistanceToCircle(RevolvedPoint(p, 0.0), radius).LawEq(DistanceToSphere(p, radius));
```

### Law_CircleIsSphereSlice

[stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato, line 115](../../../../../stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato#L115)

```plato
// A circle is the z = 0 slice of the sphere of the same radius.
Law_CircleIsSphereSlice(p: Point2D, radius: Number): Boolean
    => DistanceToCircle(p, radius).LawEq(DistanceToSphere(Point3D(p.X, p.Y, 0.0), radius));
```

```plato

    //==
    // # Planar signed distance primitives
    //
    // The planar half of the primitive family, under the same portability rules as
    // the spatial one above: scalar and fixed-arity vector arithmetic only. Each is
    // the 2D counterpart of a spatial primitive — circle to sphere, ring to torus,
    // line to plane — except that the 2D box already serves as the cylinder, which
    // is why there is no separate planar capped-cylinder form.

    // The signed distance from a point to a circle of the given radius centred at
    // the origin. Exact. (IQ: sdCircle.)
    DistanceToCircle(p: Point2D, radius: Number): Number
        => p.PositionVector.Magnitude - radius;
```
